title.en: Tile Programming for GPUs
title.zh: GPU 的 Tile 编程
title.fr: Tile Programming for GPUs

content.en:
Parallel programming can be intimidating, but doesn't need to be! There's a new paradigm for parallel programming that's newcomer-friendly, highly productive, and performant: tile-based programming models.

In this example-driven talk, we'll introduce you to tile-based programming in Python, C++, and Rust. We'll present cuTile, NVIDIA's new tile programming stack and Tile IR, the new compiler stack that it is built with. You'll learn all about new features of CUDA Tile that have recently been announced, including multi-GPU communication, interoperability with traditional CUDA SIMT, and support for more diverse kernels like convolutions and stencils. We'll compare and contrast tile-based models with traditional parallel programming models. You'll see examples from a variety of domains, including HPC stencils, a sparse matrix vector (SPMV) and conjugate gradient (CG) solver, and AI models from TileGym.

By the end of the session, you'll understand how tile programming enables more intuitive, portable, and efficient development of high-performance, data-parallel applications, for HPC, data science, and machine learning.
content.zh:
并行编程不一定令人望而生畏！Tile 编程模型是一种对新手友好、高效且性能卓越的全新并行编程范式。

本演讲将通过丰富示例，带您了解 Python、C++ 和 Rust 中的 Tile 编程。我们将介绍 NVIDIA 全新的 Tile 编程栈 cuTile 及其底层编译器栈 Tile IR，并讲解 CUDA Tile 最新特性，包括多 GPU 通信、与传统 CUDA SIMT 的互操作性，以及对卷积、模板等多样化算子的支持。演讲涵盖 HPC 模板、稀疏矩阵向量乘（SPMV）、共轭梯度（CG）求解器及 TileGym AI 模型等多领域示例。
content.fr:
La programmation parallèle n'a pas besoin d'être intimidante ! Les modèles de programmation par tuiles constituent un nouveau paradigme convivial, productif et performant.

Cet exposé axé sur des exemples présente la programmation par tuiles en Python, C++ et Rust. Nous présenterons cuTile, la nouvelle pile de programmation par tuiles de NVIDIA, et Tile IR, la pile de compilateurs sur laquelle elle repose. Vous découvrirez les nouvelles fonctionnalités de CUDA Tile, incluant la communication multi-GPU, l'interopérabilité avec CUDA SIMT traditionnel, et le support de noyaux diversifiés comme les convolutions et les stencils.

title.en: Eclipse PanEval: Architecting Neutral AI Evaluation for the Era of the EU AI Act
title.zh: Eclipse PanEval：为欧盟人工智能法时代构建中立的 AI 评估体系
title.fr: Eclipse PanEval : Concevoir une évaluation neutre de l'IA à l'ère de l'AI Act

content.en:
As Large Language Models (LLMs) transition into critical infrastructure, the requirement for transparent, reproducible evaluation becomes a regulatory necessity. This session introduces Eclipse PanEval, a community-led project recently onboarded to the Eclipse Foundation. Based on a foundational technical contribution from the FlagEval project at BAAI, Eclipse PanEval provides a vendor-neutral framework designed to help the ecosystem meet the transparency and documentation mandates of landmark regulations like the EU AI Act. We will discuss the project’s independent governance model and how its de-coupled architecture enables global technical synchronization while remaining adaptable to regional standards.
Detailed Description:
In the current AI landscape, evaluation is often fragmented. This session explores the technical architecture and open governance of Eclipse PanEval, an initiative dedicated to standardizing AI transparency through neutral stewardship.
Attendees will learn about:
1. The Onboarding of PanEval: How a sophisticated codebase was transitioned into a foundation-hosted project to ensure long-term, community-led development.
2. Neutrality by Design: Why vendor-neutral stewardship is essential for benchmarking platforms to be trusted by both developers and regulators.
3. The Infrastructure of Trust: A technical look at the project's "evaluation-as-a-service" architecture, which supports high-concurrency, multi-dimensional scoring (safety, bias, and robustness) beyond simple accuracy.
4. De-risking through De-coupling: How the project maintains technical independence, allowing the European-hosted codebase to evolve according to specific regional requirements while facilitating the bi-directional exchange of features and improvements.
Key Takeaways:
• Understand the role of neutral evaluation frameworks in demonstrating transparency for General-Purpose AI (GPAI).
• Discover how to participate in a meritocratic, open-source project focused on AI reliability.
• Learn how cross-institutional collaboration can build a decentralized standard for AI benchmarking.

title.en: Keynote – Symposium: Embracing the Ecosystem
title.zh: Keynote – Symposium：拥抱生态系统
title.fr: Keynote – Symposium : Embrasser l'écosystème

content.en:
The Rust world moves quickly, and that's only become more true with agents writing more and more code. Frontier models know Rust basics well, but they struggle when presented with new patterns that weren't present in their training data — new language features, new libraries, idioms that diverge from the familiar. The crate authors and language designers who know best how to help have no way to reach in and guide the agent.

This talk introduces Symposium, an open-source system that changes that. Symposium lets crate authors ship skills, tools, and guidance alongside their code — so adding a dependency doesn't just give your agent new APIs to call, it gives your agent the knowledge to use them well. I'll show you how it works and discuss what it means to bring Rust's decentralized, composable ecosystem model to AI tooling.

title.en: Keynote – From ChatGPT to OpenClaw: How Agentic AI is Redefining AI Compute and the Open Evaluation
title.zh: Keynote – 从 ChatGPT 到 OpenClaw：Agentic AI 如何重新定义 AI 计算与开放评估
title.fr: Keynote – De ChatGPT à OpenClaw : comment l'IA agentique redéfinit le calcul IA et l'évaluation ouverte

content.en:
The evolution from ChatGPT's conversational AI to OpenClaw's autonomous agent ecosystem marks a paradigm shift in AI compute. This transformation is fundamentally bidirectional: while advanced compute infrastructure enables increasingly sophisticated agentic capabilities, the agentic paradigm itself is reshaping compute delivery through modular, skill-based architectures.

OpenClaw exemplifies this new wave, where agentic AI system capabilities are determined by the interplay of large models, skills, and agent systems. This tripartite architecture demands new evaluation methodologies that assess not just model performance, but the orchestration of skills and autonomous decision-making—addressed by open evaluation initiatives like FlagEval and the Eclipse partnership PanEval.

FlagOS sits at the center of this transformation, building universal and inclusive AI compute capabilities that support heterogeneous hardware backends. By enabling efficient execution of the massive token volumes demanded by agentic workflows, FlagOS provides the computational substrate for this new era—where compute is not merely consumed by intelligence, but actively shaped by it.

In this talk, we will share insights on how to architect AI infrastructure for the agentic era, including the latest evaluation methodologies for agentic AI systems that go beyond traditional benchmarks to assess skill orchestration and autonomous decision-making. We will demonstrate how FlagOS Open Compute enables bidirectional empowerment: powering OpenClaw's universally accessible capabilities through cross-chip unified deployment, while OpenClaw agents feed back into FlagOS via automated operator generation and model migration. We will also discuss the path toward open, transparent evaluation standards that ensure trustworthy autonomous systems.

title.en: Keynote – The Left Brain of AI: Why Structured Data Is AI's Next Frontier
title.zh: Keynote – AI的左脑：为什么结构化数据是AI的下一个前沿
title.fr: Keynote – Le cerveau gauche de l'IA : pourquoi les données structurées sont la prochaine frontière

content.en:
Over the past three years, LLMs have transformed how organizations interact with unstructured data like text, images, code, and video. But the majority of valuable enterprise data is structured in millions of rows and columns of tabular data: transaction logs, ERPs, CRMs etc. It's these datasets that underpin every critical enterprise decision.

Until now enterprises have relied on antiquated ML algorithms to leverage these tabular datasets to make predictions and inform decisions. This is a slow and inaccurate process.

In this keynote, Alexandre Gerbeaux explores how Large Tabular Models (LTMs) solve this problem, and why LTMs are emerging as the next major category in AI given their promise to unlock trillions of dollars of value that have been locked in tables. He'll explain why structured data has remained one of AI's biggest blind spots, how LTMs differ from traditional machine learning and LLM architectures, and why predictive AI is entering its own foundation model era.

Through real-world examples in finance, healthcare, insurance, and manufacturing, Alexandre will show how organizations are moving from experimentation to deployment — and why this shift creates a massive new opportunity for data scientists, machine learning engineers, and forward deployed engineers.

The future of enterprise AI isn't generative — it's predictive.

content.en: Brain foundation models trained on massive brain data can convert thoughts into texts and images. This was impossible until a few years ago. This talk explores how large-scale pretrained models are enabling a new generation of non-invasive brain-computer interfaces, transforming raw neural signals into language and imagery with unprecedented accuracy.

content.fr: Des modèles de fondation cérébraux entraînés sur des données cérébrales massives peuvent convertir les pensées en textes et images. Cet exposé explore comment les modèles pré-entraînés à grande échelle permettent une nouvelle génération d'interfaces cerveau-ordinateur non invasives.

title.en: Beyond the Chatbot: Building Autonomous Agent Ecosystems with Minimax

title.fr: Au-delà du chatbot : construire des écosystèmes d'agents autonomes avec Minimax

content.en:
The era of the chatbot is giving way to something more powerful: autonomous agent ecosystems where AI systems proactively plan, coordinate, and execute complex workflows with minimal human intervention. Minimax has been at the forefront of this transition, developing models and infrastructure that power agent-native applications at scale.

This talk examines what it takes to move beyond simple question-and-answer interactions toward multi-step agentic pipelines — the model capabilities required, the tooling and orchestration layers needed, and the real-world challenges of deploying autonomous agents in production. Attendees will learn how Minimax approaches the agent ecosystem problem and what the next wave of AI-powered applications looks like.
content.zh:
聊天机器人时代正让位于更强大的事物：自主 Agent 生态系统，AI 系统在其中主动规划、协调和执行复杂工作流，无需大量人工干预。Minimax 一直站在这一转变的前沿，开发支持大规模 Agent 原生应用的模型和基础设施。

本演讲探讨如何从简单问答交互迈向多步骤 Agentic 流程——所需的模型能力、工具和编排层，以及在生产环境中部署自主 Agent 的现实挑战。
content.fr:
L'ère du chatbot cède la place à quelque chose de plus puissant : les écosystèmes d'agents autonomes où les systèmes IA planifient, coordonnent et exécutent des workflows complexes avec un minimum d'intervention humaine. Minimax est à l'avant-garde de cette transition.

Cette présentation examine ce qu'il faut pour aller au-delà des interactions simples vers des pipelines agentiques multi-étapes — les capacités de modèles requises, les couches d'outillage et d'orchestration nécessaires, et les défis réels du déploiement d'agents autonomes en production.

title.en: Pie: A Programmable Serving System for Agentic Applications
title.zh: Pie：面向 Agentic 应用的可编程服务系统
title.fr: Pie : Un système de service programmable pour les applications agentiques

content.en:
Emerging large language model (LLM) applications involve diverse reasoning strategies and agentic workflows, straining the capabilities of existing serving systems built on a monolithic token generation loop. This talk presents Pie, a programmable LLM serving system designed for flexibility and efficiency.

Pie decomposes the traditional generation loop into fine-grained service handlers exposed via an API and delegates control of the generation process to user-provided programs called inferlets. This enables applications to implement new KV cache strategies, bespoke generation logic, and seamlessly integrate computation and I/O—entirely within the application, without requiring modifications to the serving system.

Pie executes inferlets using WebAssembly, benefiting from its lightweight sandboxing. Evaluation shows Pie improves latency and throughput by 1.3×–3.4× on agentic workflows. Pie is open-source at pie-project.org.
content.zh: 新兴 LLM 应用涉及多样化推理策略与 Agentic 工作流，现有基于单体 Token 生成循环的服务系统难以胜任。Pie 是一个可编程 LLM 服务系统，将传统生成循环分解为细粒度服务处理器，通过用户自定义程序（inferlet）控制生成过程，在 Agentic 工作流上实现 1.3×–3.4× 的延迟与吞吐量提升。
content.fr: Pie est un système de service LLM programmable qui décompose la boucle de génération traditionnelle en gestionnaires de services à grain fin, permettant aux applications d'implémenter de nouvelles stratégies de cache KV et une logique de génération sur mesure. Pie améliore la latence et le débit de 1,3× à 3,4×.

title.en: Linear Attention: Past, Present and Future
title.zh: Linear Attention: Past, Present and Future
title.fr: Linear Attention: Past, Present and Future

speakers.name: Minako Kojima
speakers.title: Head of Developer Relations, Moonshot AI

content.en: The quadratic complexity of standard self-attention has become the fundamental bottleneck for long-context AI agents and edge-deployed models. Linear attention mechanisms—transforming the attention computation from O(n²) to O(n)—have emerged as one of the most significant algorithmic breakthroughs in efficient sequence modeling. This talk presents a comprehensive technical journey through the evolution of linear attention, from theoretical foundations (Performer, Linear Transformer, RNN reformulations) through current state-of-the-art architectures (Mamba, RetNet, GLA), and concludes with critical research frontiers: hybrid attention strategies for agentic workflows, hardware-software co-design for edge deployment, and the convergence of linear attention with state-space models. Drawing from production experience training large-scale foundation models, this session bridges algorithmic innovation with infrastructure reality.

title.en: Beyond the Chatbot: Building Autonomous Agent Ecosystems with Minimax
title.zh: 超越聊天机器人：与 Minimax 一起构建自主智能体生态系统
title.fr: Au-delà du chatbot : construire des écosystèmes d'agents autonomes avec Minimax

content.en: As the AI landscape shifts from 'Model-Centric' experimentation to 'System-Centric' deployment, the true value of Large Language Models lies in their ability to act as autonomous agents. In this session, we explore how Minimax is bridging this gap, with industry-leading context windows for complex reasoning, cost-effective high-concurrency inference, and native multimodal capabilities. Through concrete case studies, we demonstrate how Minimax transforms static models into dynamic, task-solving systems, and how to leverage open standards and Minimax's architecture to build scalable, reliable, and sovereign AI solutions.

title.en: World Model for Universal Generation and Control
title.zh: World Model for Universal Generation and Control
title.fr: World Model for Universal Generation and Control

content.en: In AI and cognitive science, world models are key for planning, reasoning, and learning from experience. We develop a flow matching and DPO reinforcement learning framework to improve the continuity and physical awareness in world model representation and generation, achieving best-of-the-results in physical awareness and state-of-the-art in open-source video generation. We also develop a comprehensive physical awareness benchmarking and arena system, extracting 50-60 metrics demonstrating physical law awareness of video generation and trajectory — covering common sense, Newtonian mechanics, optics, energy, chemical, and materials. We also describe our effort towards the concept of "world model for all", which utilizes a single world model for robotic control, navigation, task management, planning, and automatic SLAM and 3D reconstruction for environment sensing.

title.en: OpenSeek-10B: Scaling Open-Source LLMs with Less Compute
title.zh: OpenSeek-10B: Scaling Open-Source LLMs with Less Compute
title.fr: OpenSeek-10B: Scaling Open-Source LLMs with Less Compute

speakers.name: Jiabei Chen
speakers.title: Core Contributor, OpenSeek, BAAI; Ph.D. Student, CASIA

content.en: Pretraining large language models from scratch is expensive — but does it have to be? In this talk, we present OpenSeek-10B, a fully open-source 10B-parameter language model that outperforms Qwen3-14B-Base and other open-source models of comparable size, while reducing pretraining FLOPs by roughly 20x. We share two key techniques: small-model initialization, which grows a well-trained 4B model to 10B scale through hybrid width-depth expansion; and the Muon optimizer, which further accelerates training convergence over AdamW. Combined with a carefully designed multi-stage data strategy built entirely on open-source datasets, we provide a practical, reproducible blueprint for the community to pretrain competitive models at lower cost. We also share how FlagOS, BAAI's open-source unified software stack validated across chips from 6 vendors, enables this recipe to run efficiently beyond a single hardware ecosystem.

title.en: Building the World's First Open-Source Multimodal Speedrun Model

speakers.title: Board Chairperson, LF AI & Data Foundation; Huawei

content.en: Standing on the shoulders of giants like modded-nanogpt speedrun and marin speedrun, the Open Model Initiative under LFAI&Data Foundation kickstarted a new speedrun effort focusing on multi-modal models in early 2026. This is the first effort to accelerate model architecture and training/inference innovation for multi-modal tasks worldwide. In this talk we will share the motivation for this effort, how it came about and the latest submission we have received since launch of the effort.

title.en: Exploring HiFloat8: A Tapered Format Complementing the FP8 Ecosystem for Robust Model Training
title.zh: Exploring HiFloat8: A Tapered Format Complementing the FP8 Ecosystem for Robust Model Training
title.fr: Exploring HiFloat8: A Tapered Format Complementing the FP8 Ecosystem for Robust Model Training

content.en: The quantization to FP8 formats has significantly accelerated LLM training. Standard FP8 formats suffer from frequent gradient overflows and heavy reliance on complex dynamic scaling (Delayed Scaling), which often lead to training instability in billion-parameter models. This session introduces HiFloat8 (HiF8) — a tapered precision format that offers an alternative approach to managing dynamic range. We demonstrate the implementation of HiF8 within the PyTorch ecosystem and analyze training stability and final loss parity, highlighting specific scenarios where HiF8 provides relatively the same accuracy and 1.5–1.7× GEMM performance compared to FP16.

title.en: When Does Sparsity Mitigate the Curse of Depth in LLMs
title.zh: When Does Sparsity Mitigate the Curse of Depth in LLMs
title.fr: When Does Sparsity Mitigate the Curse of Depth in LLMs

speakers.name: Shiwei Liu
speakers.title: Group Leader, Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems; PI, ELLIS Institute Tübingen

content.en: Recent work has demonstrated the curse of depth in large language models, where later layers contribute less to learning than earlier layers. In this paper, we demonstrate that sparsity, beyond enabling efficiency, acts as a regulator of variance propagation and thereby improves depth utilization. Our investigation covers implicit sparsity (weight decay, attention sparsity from long-context inputs) and explicit sparsity (Grouped-Query Attention, Mixture-of-Experts). Across settings, we observe a consistent relationship: sparsity improves layer utilization by reducing output variance and promoting functional differentiation. We distill our findings into a practical recipe for training depth-effective LLMs, yielding a notable 4.6% accuracy improvement on downstream tasks.

title.en: Building Scalable LLM Inference Infrastructure
title.zh: Building Scalable LLM Inference Infrastructure
title.fr: Building Scalable LLM Inference Infrastructure

speakers.name: Xingda Wei
speakers.title: Associate Professor, Shanghai Jiao Tong University

content.en: LLM serving infrastructure has become a key pillar for modern society, but building scalable LLM infrastructure remains challenging at scale due to system issues like load imbalancing, stragglers and lack of elasticity. In this talk, we will present our recent work on scalable and efficient LLM infrastructure, including simple but efficient multiplication-based LLM global router and ultra-fast autoscaling mechanisms. Some of these works have been or are being deployed on world's largest LLM service providers.

title.en: Writing Rust AI Applications with Makepad
title.zh: Writing Rust AI Applications with Makepad
title.fr: Writing Rust AI Applications with Makepad

content.en: In this talk we will show how to rapidly create high performance Rust applications with Makepad. You can use your AI of choice — codex, claude — running inside the makepad IDE. Rust is the ideal language for AI generation because of its strong compiler guarantees and superb performance. Makepad studio has automation integration for the AI so it can generate, see, click buttons and iterate completely automated on visual applications. Makepad compiles to web, desktop, mobile, and XR. We will demo how far we can push AI application generation including AI generated CAD, 3D, map rendering, vector engines, and mixed reality 3D world scanning.

title.en: Software Factory: Stop Looking at the Code
title.zh: 软件工厂：别再看代码了
title.fr: Software Factory : Arrêtez de regarder le code

content.en: This talk explores building with StrongDM's Attractor: a multi-agent orchestrator capable of delivering production-ready features by walking a graph of nodes. We've used the tool internally to deliver drivers for cloud databases, and it proved its worth for simple compiler development and complicated numerical analysis algorithm tasks. The specification is open source.

title.en: Building Agentic Apps with CopilotKit and AG-UI
title.zh: Building Agentic Apps with CopilotKit and AG-UI
title.fr: Building Agentic Apps with CopilotKit and AG-UI

content.en: AI agents are reshaping how users interact with software. This talk explores Agentic UX through AG-UI, an open protocol that standardizes agent-to-user interactions, enabling intuitive, real-time, and collaborative AI experiences. We'll explore lessons from building AG-UI, an open, event-based protocol that standardizes agent-to-user communication, covering the AG-UI event model, human-in-the-loop patterns, and how vendor-neutral messaging enables interoperability across frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI, and Mastra.

title.en: AgentChat: Cross-Server Communication for Humans and Agents
title.zh: AgentChat：面向人类和智能体的跨服务器通信
title.fr: AgentChat : Communication inter-serveurs pour humains et agents

content.en:
As AI agents become more capable, the next challenge is not only how to run a single agent, but how humans and multiple agents can communicate in a shared, persistent environment.

AgentChat is an open-source communication platform for humans and agents. It provides a messaging kernel that supports direct messages, group chats, persistent identities, and message delivery across local runtimes, devices, and servers. Agents running on the same machine can coordinate with each other, agents on different devices can stay connected, and my agent can directly collaborate with your agent without requiring humans to manually relay context between systems.

The goal of AgentChat is not to define what every agent should do, but to provide the platform they can use to communicate, coordinate, and stay connected. Matrix can be used as one frontend because it is open and controllable, but AgentChat is not tied to Matrix itself. It has its own communication core and can serve as a general substrate for human-agent and agent-agent interaction.

On top of this platform, developers can build many higher-level workflows, such as delegation, collaborative coding, monitoring, or human-in-the-loop operations. But the foundation remains the same: a common communication layer where humans and agents are first-class participants, whether they are running locally or across distributed environments.

In this talk, I will introduce the design of AgentChat, explain why agent communication needs to go beyond single-user and single-device setups, and share lessons from building an open platform for direct, structured, and persistent collaboration among humans and agents.

title.en: Vibe Native for More: Why AI Agents Deserve a Better App Framework
title.zh: Vibe Native for More: Why AI Agents Deserve a Better App Framework
title.fr: Vibe Native for More: Why AI Agents Deserve a Better App Framework

content.en: AI is transforming how apps are built, but not what they're built on. Without a cross-platform framework, agents must generate, verify, and maintain separate code for every platform. This talk introduces Lynx, the open-source cross-platform framework powering TikTok and CapCut at billion-user scale, and our three principles for AI-native app infrastructure: AI-Ergonomic (harness-able), AI-Efficient (token-economical), and AI-Expressive (intent-driven UI). We demonstrate how vue-lynx — a full Vue 3 renderer for Lynx — was vibe-coded in two weeks as proof of this principle.

title.en: Self-Evolving Apps: Building Software That Gets Smarter Every Time You Use It
title.zh: Self-Evolving Apps: Building Software That Gets Smarter Every Time You Use It
title.fr: Self-Evolving Apps: Building Software That Gets Smarter Every Time You Use It

content.en:
Most apps are built once and stay the same. Self-evolving apps are different, they improve every time you use them, not because someone updates the code, but because the app learns from your corrections.

This intelligence exists completely outside the app as a separate, updatable layer. Before each use, it reads your previous corrections and uses them as examples to make better decisions. No machine learning required, neither retraining or data science team. In this session, I will walk you through what self-evolving apps are, how to design them, how to build one, which licensing models work best and the lessons I have learned from building several of these apps, as well as a live demonstration.

title.en: From LLM Apps to Agent Systems: Building an AI Operating System with Octos
title.zh: From LLM Apps to Agent Systems: Building an AI Operating System with Octos
title.fr: From LLM Apps to Agent Systems: Building an AI Operating System with Octos

content.en:
What if you could design agents like Socrates' daimonion — not one, but many? A beacon that watches your project evolve and generates a slide deck before Monday's meeting. Another that curates your morning news into a personalized radio station, read aloud in your preferred voice. A third orchestrating a research pipeline overnight with eight workers fanning out in parallel. Each arm thinking independently, all sharing one brain.

Octos — the Open Cognitive Tasks Orchestration System — makes this architecture real. A single 31MB Rust binary that serves 200+ users on a Mac Mini. No Python, no Docker, no runtime dependencies. 15 LLM providers with 3-layer failover so your daimons never go silent. 12 messaging channels so they meet people where they already are. Three memory layers so they remember what matters. And smart tool management that keeps agents sharp — 30+ capabilities available, but only 15 active at any moment, like an octopus choosing which arms to extend.

In this talk, we'll explore the design principles behind building agent applications that transcend chat — from multi-channel presence to proactive orchestration, from provider resilience to the hard problem of giving an agent many arms without losing its mind.

You'll leave with a new mental model: agents not as tools you use, but as daimons you design.

title.en: Accelerating the Distributed Ecosystem: AI-Powered Scaling for Oniro
title.zh: Accelerating the Distributed Ecosystem: AI-Powered Scaling for Oniro
title.fr: Accelerating the Distributed Ecosystem: AI-Powered Scaling for Oniro

content.en: Scaling a modern OS ecosystem requires massive developer velocity. This session explores how the Eclipse Oniro project leverages AI as a "force multiplier" to rapidly build out its landscape, streamlining the porting of popular apps and integrating modern frameworks into the OpenHarmony environment. We share practical insights into how AI-assisted engineering allows us to bridge different frameworks and create new applications in a fraction of the usual time, while maintaining CRA compliance and tracking emerging initiatives like Unified Attestation.

title.en: AI Companion is the New Interface: Building a Learning Agent Device with China's Hardware Ecosystem
title.zh: AI Companion is the New Interface: Building a Learning Agent Device with China's Hardware Ecosystem
title.fr: AI Companion is the New Interface: Building a Learning Agent Device with China's Hardware Ecosystem

content.en: AI is rapidly evolving from chatbots to copilots, and now toward agent-based systems. But most AI experiences still live inside apps — fragmented, reactive, and short-lived. This talk introduces a new paradigm: AI companions that combine agent intelligence, multimodal interaction (voice and vision), and hardware to support continuous, personalized learning. Drawing from the journey from Microsoft Copilot and Agent product leadership to building Ingora, an AI-native learning companion for children, the talk explores why traditional 'AI tutor' models fall short, and how inquiry-driven interaction, emotional engagement, and long-horizon agent design can reshape learning experiences.

title.en: From LLM Calls to Governed Agent Systems: Building a Runtime for Auditability, Replay, and Control
title.zh: From LLM Calls to Governed Agent Systems: Building a Runtime for Auditability, Replay, and Control
title.fr: From LLM Calls to Governed Agent Systems: Building a Runtime for Auditability, Replay, and Control

speakers.name: Tianyi Han
speakers.title: Architect Solution, AI Systems & Agent Governance, Capgemini

content.en: As AI systems evolve from isolated LLM calls into autonomous agents, a new class of engineering problems emerges: lack of control, limited observability, and no reliable way to audit or reproduce decisions. In this talk, we introduce a governance-oriented runtime for AI agents providing policy enforcement, trace-based auditability, deterministic replay, and evaluation hooks for non-regression. By treating agent execution as a structured, observable, and controllable process, we enable developers to move from "best-effort prompting" to "engineered agent systems" that are auditable, reproducible, and production-ready.

title.en: Agents, Code & Parallel Worlds — The 300-Day Agentic Evolution of Cangjie Programming Language Team — Agentic OS & App
title.zh: Agents, Code & Parallel Worlds — The 300-Day Agentic Evolution of Cangjie Programming Language Team — Agentic OS & App
title.fr: Agents, Code & Parallel Worlds — The 300-Day Agentic Evolution of Cangjie Programming Language Team — Agentic OS & App

speakers.name: Sean Dong
speakers.title: Program Director, Central Software Institute, Huawei

content.en: This topic describes the complete process of Cangjie's 300-day AI R&D transformation, starting with an accidental AI coding attempt in May 2025. The team gradually implemented the Agent Centric Engineering (ACE) model, selected 30% of the teams to pilot end-to-end AI, and achieved dramatic productivity gains: the compiler team improved by 240–2600%, the third-party library team by 132–816%, and the standard library team by 125%. This talk passes on the core concept of "actively embracing AI, breaking the shackles of thinking, and realizing the reconstruction of individual and team values."

title.en: Who Controls Your Agents? Building Vendor-Neutral Infrastructure for Agentic Developer Tools
title.zh: Who Controls Your Agents? Building Vendor-Neutral Infrastructure for Agentic Developer Tools
title.fr: Who Controls Your Agents? Building Vendor-Neutral Infrastructure for Agentic Developer Tools

speakers.name: Thomas Froment
speakers.title: Program Manager, Development Tools, Eclipse Foundation

content.en: Agentic AI is rapidly transforming developer tooling, shifting from passive assistants to autonomous agents acting across the software lifecycle. Yet many systems, while marketed as open, still depend on single-vendor governance and opaque AI integrations. This session presents a practical alternative built within the Eclipse Foundation, introducing Theia AI — an open source framework for agentic capabilities in developer tools with multi-LLM orchestration and full control over model selection — and Open VSX, an open source extension registry enabling transparent distribution of agent integrations. Together they provide a vendor-neutral foundation for building and governing agentic developer systems, with over 300 million extension downloads per month.

title.en: Bridging the Chasm: Practical AI Experiments in the Servo Engine
title.zh: Bridging the Chasm: Practical AI Experiments in the Servo Engine
title.fr: Bridging the Chasm: Practical AI Experiments in the Servo Engine

content.en: Can AI-assisted coding significantly accelerate the implementation of complex web standards? This talk explores a series of experiments on a fork of the Servo web engine, aimed at closing the feature gap with dominant engines. We explore two approaches: treating AI as a high-speed implementation partner for an architect with deep system knowledge but limited domain expertise (WebNN), and using test-driven AI where rigorous Web Platform Tests steer an AI through a black-box implementation (CSS Grid).

title.en: The Web Was Built for Humans — Agents Broke It. Now We Need Agentic Apps
title.zh: The Web Was Built for Humans — Agents Broke It. Now We Need Agentic Apps
title.fr: The Web Was Built for Humans — Agents Broke It. Now We Need Agentic Apps

content.en: The web was built for humans — clicks, forms, and visual flows. But today, a new class of users has emerged: AI agents. These agents don't browse your application — they operate it. This talk introduces the concept of agentic applications, defined not by their UI but by the capabilities they expose. We explore how this shift is happening through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), and present WebMCP — an approach to turning web applications into programmable systems. Using real examples from React apps, we show how existing UI logic can be exposed as structured, composable capabilities, allowing agents to interact with your app directly without brittle selectors or reverse engineering.

title.en: One Year of llama.cpp: Milestones and Future Plans
title.zh: One Year of llama.cpp: Milestones and Future Plans
title.fr: One Year of llama.cpp: Milestones and Future Plans

content.en: Reflect on llama.cpp's journey from mid-2025 to mid-2026, highlighting key achievements: the new Web UI, support for popular models like GPT-OSS and Qwen3.5, key performance improvements, and integrations with downstream applications like LM Studio and LlamaBarn. Looking ahead, we'll discuss upcoming features and collaborative roadmaps to push open-source AI further. llama.cpp has revolutionized efficient LLM inference on consumer hardware, enabling accessible AI for developers worldwide.

title.en: Bridging AI Ecosystems: RustNN as a Universal WebNN Implementation
title.zh: Bridging AI Ecosystems: RustNN as a Universal WebNN Implementation
title.fr: Bridging AI Ecosystems: RustNN as a Universal WebNN Implementation

content.en: The emergence of WebNN offers a massive opportunity to unify the AI landscape through a single, high-performance standard that runs everywhere. RustNN is growing into a robust, native Rust implementation of the WebNN specification that meets ML developers where they are today. In this session, we'll demonstrate how RustNN creates a unified pipeline for the AI ecosystem: using ONNX and Torch converters to pull models from the Python research environment; how the RustNN core targets CoreML, TensorRT, and WebAssembly; and how Python and Node.js bindings allow teams to use the same Rust-powered engine across their entire stack.

title.en: Khal and Inferi: Towards Single-Language Cross-Platform GPU Inference with Rust and rust-gpu
title.zh: Khal and Inferi: Towards Single-Language Cross-Platform GPU Inference with Rust and rust-gpu
title.fr: Khal and Inferi: Towards Single-Language Cross-Platform GPU Inference with Rust and rust-gpu

content.en: After multiple technological explorations for cross-platform GPU programming like WGSL and Slang, we present our latest experiment with a codebase where both CPU code and GPU kernels are written with the same language: Rust. By leveraging cargo and the rust compiler (through rust-gpu), we implemented common tensor and LLM inference operators running on all major platforms, including the web. The benefit of writing regular Rust code, strong typing across the GPU/CPU boundary, and the Cargo package manager enable smooth integration with codebases across multiple domains for AI and beyond.

title.en: Rewriting Agent Infrastructure in Rust
title.zh: Rewriting Agent Infrastructure in Rust
title.fr: Rewriting Agent Infrastructure in Rust

content.en: AI agents are only as good as the tools they call. We make the case for Rust as the default language for agent tooling: single-binary, zero dependencies, memory safe, and runs anywhere. Lessons learned from porting real AI capabilities into standalone Rust CLI tools — what the process looks like, which parts of the Rust ecosystem are production-ready, and how to think about the boundary between Python (where your models live) and Rust (where your tooling should live).

title.en: KTransformers: Full-Precision Inference for 600B+ MoE Models on Consumer Hardware
title.zh: KTransformers: Full-Precision Inference for 600B+ MoE Models on Consumer Hardware
title.fr: KTransformers: Full-Precision Inference for 600B+ MoE Models on Consumer Hardware

content.en: KTransformers is an open-source CPU-GPU heterogeneous inference framework that runs frontier MoE models like DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen3.5-397B at FP8 precision on consumer GPUs. By offloading expert computations to CPU with CUDA Graph-capturable coordination, it achieves 35+ tokens/sec decode speed — making 600B+ models accessible without datacenter infrastructure.

title.zh: Power Every Smart Device with Intelligence
title.fr: Power Every Smart Device with Intelligence

speakers.name: Chenzhe Jing
speakers.title: Director of Modelbest OSPO, OpenBMB Operation Lead

content.en: The presentation will primarily focus on the technical details of ModelBest's on-device large models — MiniCPM & MiniCPM-o — as well as their real-world applications across smart cockpits, smartphones, smart home devices, and robotics.

title.en: OminiX: Fully Automated Native C++ Deployment for Diverse Large-Scale Learning Models
title.zh: OminiX: Fully Automated Native C++ Deployment for Diverse Large-Scale Learning Models
title.fr: OminiX: Fully Automated Native C++ Deployment for Diverse Large-Scale Learning Models

content.en: Running deep learning inference in native C++ enables efficient edge deployment, eliminates Python/PyTorch dependencies, and allows fast, accurate quantization. We propose OminiX cpp, an automated pipeline where an AI agent with structured procedural skills converts arbitrary PyTorch models into optimized C++ inference code targeting the GGML runtime. OminiX cpp generalizes beyond LLMs to support diverse model families including image and video generation, speech recognition, text-to-speech, world models, and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models.

title.en: Vulkan for Edge AI: Expanding the Hardware Frontier with llama.cpp
title.zh: Vulkan for Edge AI: Expanding the Hardware Frontier with llama.cpp
title.fr: Vulkan for Edge AI: Expanding the Hardware Frontier with llama.cpp

speakers.name: Ruben Ortlam
speakers.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Red Hat

content.en: Agentic AI on the edge requires accessible, low-latency inference, yet hardware fragmentation limits deployment. While CUDA dominates acceleration, its vendor lock-in constrains local intelligence. This talk examines Vulkan as a vendor-neutral alternative, showcasing how it expanded compatibility and reduced deployment complexity in llama.cpp across Intel, AMD, and Nvidia GPUs. We outline engineering roadblocks and explore VK_NV_cooperative_matrix2 as a blueprint for offloading hardware-specific optimizations to the driver, enabling peak performance via vendor optimizations while supporting broad hardware through generic shader fallbacks.

title.en: RoboChallenge Annual Report on Large-Scale Real Robot Benchmark
title.zh: RoboChallenge Annual Report on Large-Scale Real Robot Benchmark
title.fr: RoboChallenge Annual Report on Large-Scale Real Robot Benchmark

content.en: In early 2026, RoboChallenge released the world's first large-scale evaluation leaderboard for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models based on real robot environments. The data shows exponential growth in both registered users and evaluation submissions. Currently, the top-ranked model achieves around 62% success rate on the Table30 task suite, while performance on fine-grained manipulation tasks remains below 15%. The platform has attracted developers from multiple countries, with the majority of top-performing models being open source — underscoring that open collaboration is a key driver in advancing embodied intelligence.

title.en: LeRobot Humanoide: An Open Source 3D Printed Robot
title.zh: LeRobot Humanoide: An Open Source 3D Printed Robot
title.fr: LeRobot Humanoide: An Open Source 3D Printed Robot

content.en: We present an open-source bipedal robotic platform designed through a unified co-design methodology, integrating mechanical design, parameter optimization, and control. The robot is almost entirely fabricated using additive manufacturing, relying on 3D-printed structural components with a minimal set of off-the-shelf elements, significantly reducing cost and manufacturing complexity. The platform has been developed end-to-end with a particular focus on ensuring consistency between simulation and physical behavior. By releasing the full mechanical design, control software, and simulation tools, this work aims to provide a reproducible and extensible baseline for bipedal robotics, lowering the barrier to hardware experimentation and accelerating progress in open embodied AI.

title.en: Skill Foundry: An AI That Embodies a Robot, Watches Itself, and Learns
title.zh: Skill Foundry: An AI That Embodies a Robot, Watches Itself, and Learns
title.fr: Skill Foundry: An AI That Embodies a Robot, Watches Itself, and Learns

speakers.name: Charbel Dandjinou
speakers.title: CTO / Founder / AI Research Engineer, Reflexion Robotics

content.en: An AI embodies a simulated robot, evolves through curriculum, and collects new skills. Unlike Eureka, it sees itself — robot POV and scene cameras — then iterates on reward, strategy, and all training params. Skill Foundry is a curriculum system where an AI (Claude or any LLM) embodies a simulated robot and autonomously evolves to acquire new skills. The surprising finding: human engineer in the loop converges faster and outperforms pure AI at designing training strategies — the system works best as a human-AI collaboration.

title.en: Amazing Hand: An Open-Source Robotic Hand — Technical Report
title.zh: Amazing Hand：开源机器人手——技术报告
title.fr: Amazing Hand : Une main robotique open source — Rapport technique

content.en: Amazing Hand is an open-source robotic hand with four fingers and eight degrees of freedom. Inexpensive and easy to build yourself, it's an expressive hand based on an original mechanical design. Without cables or custom actuators, it offers a clever design and simplified handling. While it can't manipulate heavy objects, it's ideal for having fun and unleashing creativity, unlike traditional robotic grippers that lack personality.

title.en: Robotics with Zenoh: From ROS 2 to ros-z and Beyond
title.zh: Robotics with Zenoh: From ROS 2 to ros-z and Beyond
title.fr: Robotics with Zenoh: From ROS 2 to ros-z and Beyond

content.en: Eclipse Zenoh has established itself as a high-performance communication protocol for robotics: low-latency pub/sub, location-transparent routing from shared memory to WAN, built-in support for queryables, efficient bandwidth usage, and seamless peer-to-peer or routed topologies. Its adoption by ROS 2 as a Tier 1 middleware (rmw_zenoh) validated what the community had been asking for. This led to ros-z — a pure-Rust, Zenoh-native ROS 2 implementation that opens the ROS ecosystem to non-ROS environments. With support for multiple serialization formats (CDR, Protobuf, CUDA tensors) and language bindings in Rust, Python, and Go, ros-z extends its reach to communities and tech stacks traditionally outside the ROS world.

title.en: AI Agents Learn Invisible Shortcuts
title.zh: AI Agents Learn Invisible Shortcuts
title.fr: AI Agents Learn Invisible Shortcuts

content.en: Classic RL agents often achieve 'superhuman' performance not through true comprehension, but by exploiting hidden shortcuts in their environments. Much like 'Clever Hans', the horse that appeared to do arithmetic but was actually just reading human cues, our models project an illusion of competence. This talk explores the pervasive danger of shortcut learning and proposes a path forward: prioritizing interpretability. By using LLMs and neuro-symbolic approaches to distill black-box policies into transparent, human-readable programs, we can unmask these hidden flaws, audit agent behavior, and build genuinely robust AI systems.

title.en: Building Visual Navigation Foundation Models with Scalable Simulation Data
title.zh: Building Visual Navigation Foundation Models with Scalable Simulation Data
title.fr: Building Visual Navigation Foundation Models with Scalable Simulation Data

content.en: Building a general navigation system using only an external camera is a promising goal. In this talk, we introduce explorations in this direction based on scalable simulated navigation data. We elaborate on the motivation for using simulated data, present the details of constructing the data pipeline, and introduce several works on how to train a capable navigation policy with simulation data.

title.en: Can Robots Learn Surgery? Open Data, Foundation Models, and the Road to Surgical Autonomy
title.zh: Can Robots Learn Surgery? Open Data, Foundation Models, and the Road to Surgical Autonomy
title.fr: Can Robots Learn Surgery? Open Data, Foundation Models, and the Road to Surgical Autonomy

speakers.name: Jad Fayad
speakers.title: Manager of Systems & AI Engineering, Moon Surgical

content.en: Can robots learn surgery the way humans do — by observing, practicing, and improving? In this talk, we present Open-H Embodiment, an open collaboration across 35+ institutions to build the first shared data foundation for healthcare robotics. By standardizing on LeRobot, Open-H unifies 778 hours of multimodal data spanning surgical robotics, ultrasound, and endoscopy. This shared foundation enables training general Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation models like GR00T-H across diverse systems. Open standards, shared models, and community-owned infrastructure are not idealistic — they are the only viable path to scalable robotic intelligence in healthcare.

title.en: Reachy Mini: How to Have Fun with Expressive Robotics
title.zh: Reachy Mini: How to Have Fun with Expressive Robotics
title.fr: Reachy Mini: How to Have Fun with Expressive Robotics

content.en: What happens when a robot stops being just hardware and starts feeling… alive? This talk shares a hands-on journey with Reachy Mini: from first experiments to pushing its limits with custom hardware, AI integrations, and unconventional use cases. From building light-up eyes and integrating mmWave sensors for presence and vital signs, to connecting AI systems like virtual try-on models, this session dives into how small, playful experiments can unlock surprisingly powerful capabilities.

title.en: LeRobotDataset: Scaling Across Modalities
title.zh: LeRobotDataset: Scaling Across Modalities
title.fr: LeRobotDataset: Scaling Across Modalities

content.en: Most state-of-the-art robot learning datasets for manipulation rely on a limited set of modalities — task descriptions, joint states, and synchronized RGB images. This talk presents the challenges encountered when introducing new modalities into the LeRobot dataset, along with the design decisions made to balance diversity with efficiency. It discusses practical solutions for integrating heterogeneous data (audio, tactile feedback, depth) while maintaining scalable and usable dataset structures.

title.en: XLeRobot: Building an Open-Source Dual-Arm Mobile Robot for Everyone
title.zh: XLeRobot: Building an Open-Source Dual-Arm Mobile Robot for Everyone
title.fr: XLeRobot: Building an Open-Source Dual-Arm Mobile Robot for Everyone

content.en: XLeRobot is a fully open-source dual-arm mobile robot for household tasks, costing $660 in parts and under 4 hours to assemble. It combines SO-101 arms, a Lekiwi base, and an IKEA cart on top of the Hugging Face LeRobot ecosystem. Since launching in May 2025, it has reached 4.8k+ GitHub stars and a community of 6,000+ builders worldwide. This talk shares how XLeRobot grew from a PhD side project on robust manipulation into a widely adopted platform, covering the design philosophy, how it gained traction with zero promotion, and how the community has extended it — from university research testbeds to third-party assembly kits to academic papers. We also reflect on modern middleware like DORA and NVIDIA's open Physical AI stack (Isaac GR00T, Newton, Cosmos) now integrating directly into LeRobot.

title.en: The Real Challenge Isn't Starting.
title.zh: 真正的挑战不是开始
title.fr: Le vrai défi, ce n'est pas de commencer.

content.en: Starting is easy. Continuing is the hard part. I'll walk through my own journey from a struggling robotics team at 15 to building Inhabit, an open-source humanoid robot teleoperation platform, and how AI tools made it possible to ship something real as basically one person in college. title.en: Opening Remarks — vLLM Workshop
title.zh: Opening Remarks — vLLM Workshop
title.fr: Opening Remarks — vLLM Workshop

speakers.name: Erwan Gallen
speakers.title: vLLM Contributor, Senior Principal Product Manager - Generative AI, Red Hat

content.en:
Agentic AI is reshaping inference architecture. Reasoning models, long-context workflows, and multi-step agent systems put new pressure on serving stacks, which makes accelerator strategy more important than before. The challenge is no longer only to serve a model fast. It is to match the right serving architecture and the right accelerator profile to the right workload.

That is why broad accelerator support matters in vLLM. vLLM is built for high-throughput, memory-efficient inference and serving, with an architecture designed to deploy open models across different hardware environments rather than a single path. AI accelerators span familiar categories such as GPUs, NPUs, and ASIC-based designs, with CPU support still relevant for specific deployment profiles such as smaller models, edge environments, and cost-sensitive workloads. 

The session explores what that shift means in practice for teams building inference platforms. It looks at why agentic workloads make accelerator strategy more important, why broad hardware enablement matters in the vLLM ecosystem, and how platform teams can think about infrastructure choices through the lens of workload shape, prompt and context behavior, concurrency, decode latency, memory pressure, scaling patterns, and operational fit. vLLM is a strong foundation for that discussion because the project emphasizes broad hardware support, top performance, production readiness, and extensible architecture, and its serving stack includes capabilities such as high-throughput serving, distributed inference, and online and offline inference modes.  ￼

A practical framework ties accelerator decisions back to workload requirements and deployment goals, giving attendees a clearer way to think about modern inference architecture while showing how vLLM keeps the serving layer open and adaptable as workloads evolve.

title.en: Building, Testing and Contributing to vLLM: A Developer's Guide
title.zh: 构建、测试与贡献vLLM：开发者指南

speakers.name: Daniele Trifirò
speakers.title: vLLM Contributor, Principal Software Engineer, Red Hat

content.en:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized the AI landscape, and vLLM has emerged as a leading inference engine that dramatically accelerates LLM serving through innovations like PagedAttention. But how do you actually build, test, and contribute to this rapidly evolving project?

In this talk, we'll take you through vLLM's architecture and explore the practical aspects of working with this complex Python/C++ codebase. We'll start with an overview of vLLM's core optimizations including PagedAttention, then dive into the build process for different targets as well as third party hardware plugins, such as Google TPU, AWS Neuron, Intel Gaudi and more.

You'll learn about testing strategies such as performance benchmarking with GuideLLM and model evaluation using lm-evaluation-harness. We'll also cover contribution best practices to the vLLM community and how Red Hat AI Inference Server (RHAIIS) provides a trustworthy and validated platform to run LLM workflows across diverse hardware environments.

This talk passes on the core concept of "actively embracing AI, breaking the shackles of thinking, and realizing the reconstruction of individual and team values."

title.zh: 面向智能体AI的开放计算（FlagOS）
title.fr: Calcul ouvert pour l'IA agentique (FlagOS)

speakers.name: Yonghua Lin
speakers.title: Vice President and Chief Engineer, BAAI

content.en:
The evolution from ChatGPT's conversational AI to OpenClaw's autonomous agent ecosystem marks a paradigm shift in AI compute. This transformation is fundamentally bidirectional: while advanced compute infrastructure enables increasingly sophisticated agentic capabilities, the agentic paradigm itself is reshaping compute delivery through modular, skill-based architectures.

OpenClaw exemplifies this new wave, where agentic AI system capabilities are determined by the interplay of large models, skills, and agent systems. This tripartite architecture demands new evaluation methodologies that assess not just model performance, but the orchestration of skills and autonomous decision-making—addressed by open evaluation initiatives like FlagEval and the Eclipse partnership PanEval.

FlagOS sits at the center of this transformation, building universal and inclusive AI compute capabilities that support heterogeneous hardware backends. By enabling efficient execution of the massive token volumes demanded by agentic workflows, FlagOS provides the computational substrate for this new era—where compute is not merely consumed by intelligence, but actively shaped by it.

title.en: PanEval Open-Source Introduction
title.zh: PanEval开源介绍
title.fr: Introduction open-source de PanEval

speakers.name: Qigang Zhu
speakers.title: Head of Open Source Engineering, BAAI

content.en:
The fragmentation of AI accelerators has created a prohibitive engineering bottleneck. Supporting a single model across diverse hardware requires weeks of manual porting — an unmanageable N×M combinatorial explosion.
We present FlagOS, an open-source system software stack that consolidates the heterogeneous AI landscape. Core components include a unified operator library (FlagGems, 407+ ops, 25+ accelerators), a multi-target compiler (FlagTree), and a non-invasive plugin system for framework adaptation (FlagScale).
This talk centers on the symbiotic evolution of infrastructure and agents:
FlagOS powers agents. Autonomous agents demand 24/7, high-concurrency inference. FlagOS provides a stable, unified compute abstraction that masks hardware-specific complexities, ensuring reliable inference services across diverse accelerators.
Agents power FlagOS. Through FlagOS Skills — agent-executable workflow packages — we shift from "infrastructure-as-code" to "infrastructure-as-agent." AI coding agents now autonomously perform our most complex infrastructure tasks: 13-step model backporting with E2E precision validation, and MCP-driven kernel generation (99% correctness on 110-operator benchmarks).
The infrastructure is no longer just agent-ready; it is agent-built and continuously agent-improved.
BAAI is committed to global open collaboration. We have contributed PanEval to the Eclipse Foundation as a vendor-neutral AI evaluation platform.

title.en: Bridging AI Evaluation and Real-World Deployment: Place-Based Evaluation Testbeds for High-Trust Public Domains
title.zh: Bridging AI Evaluation and Real-World Deployment: Place-Based Evaluation Testbeds for High-Trust Public Domains
title.fr: Bridging AI Evaluation and Real-World Deployment: Place-Based Evaluation Testbeds for High-Trust Public Domains

content.en:
As AI systems evolve from standalone models toward tool-using, workflow-oriented, and increasingly agentic deployments, evaluation must move beyond benchmark comparison and static task scores. This presentation proposes place-based evaluation testbeds, designed through a governance-first approach, to bridge AI evaluation and real-world deployment in high-trust public domains such as culture, education, and water-linked socio-ecological contexts.

The core argument is that benchmark performance alone does not show whether a system is ready for institution-grade deployment. In real-world settings, system quality depends not only on answer accuracy, but also on traceability, robustness, auditability, documentation readiness, and safe behavior under contextual constraints. To address this gap, the talk introduces a testbed architecture based on a governed knowledge layer rather than unconstrained generation.

The proposed pipeline is: field encounter → co-curation → governed knowledge layer → AI companion → supervised feedback loop. This creates a controlled retrieval environment in which outputs can be assessed against curated sources, provenance logic, access conditions, and correction pathways. It therefore supports evaluation not only of response quality, but also of deployment-relevant properties under realistic public-facing conditions.

As an initial reference environment, the presentation uses Tihany (Hungary), a heritage- and water-linked landscape context, to illustrate how governed knowledge layers can support more controllable and accountable public-interest AI deployment. The water dimension also connects the testbed to Source2Sea: Bartók 3.0 Connectivity (2026–2031), a UN Ocean Decade Action exploring linked cultural and water systems.

The broader claim is that place-based evaluation testbeds can complement open evaluation initiatives by providing real-world environments in which model capability, system orchestration, and societal deployment readiness can be assessed together.

content.en: Standing on the shoulders of giants like modded-nanogpt speedrun and marin speedrun, the Open Model Initiative under LFAI&Data Foundation kickstarted a new speedrun effort focusing on multi-modal models in early 2026. This is the first effort to accelerate model architecture and training/inference innovation for multi-modal tasks worldwide. In this talk we will share the motivation for this effort, how it came about and the latest submission we have received since launch of the effort.

title.en: SGLang Project and Roadmap
title.zh: SGLang项目与路线图
title.fr: Projet SGLang et feuille de route

content.en:
SGLang is an open-source high-performance serving framework for LLMs and Multimodal Models, with over 24,000 GitHub stars. In this talk, we present the key design principles behind SGLang's performance.

We will discuss recent advances including native multimodal models support, speculative decoding support (Eagle3/MTP), and FP8/NVFP4 quantization on Hopper and Blackwell GPUs. We also share lessons from maintaining a fast-moving open-source project with thousands of contributors worldwide.

Attendees will gain a practical understanding of how SGLang achieves state-of-the-art throughput and latency, and how to deploy it for production LLM serving.

content.en: Diffusion models have become the backbone of modern image and video generation, but serving them efficiently remains challenging. In this talk, we introduce SGLang-Diffusion, a high-performance inference framework designed for scalable diffusion generation. We present its system architecture and key optimizations — including advanced parallelism, distributed VAE, kernel fusion, and serving improvements — that enable efficient and production-ready deployment of diffusion models. We also demonstrate how SGLang-Diffusion accelerates popular open-source models and supports large-scale multimodal generation workloads.

content.en: Reinforcement learning post-training has become a critical stage in building capable foundation models — yet most open-source practitioners still struggle to set up a stable, high-throughput RL pipeline. This hands-on lab brings SGLang's battle-tested RL infrastructure directly to participants. Attendees will walk through building an end-to-end RL training loop using SGLang as the rollout backend, learn how to integrate it with the Miles framework, and tackle real challenges like training-inference mismatch and rollout efficiency at scale. SGLang powers RL post-training for frontier models across the industry, running on over 400,000 GPUs worldwide.

title.en: The Long Game: Building Europe’s Sovereign AI Layer
title.zh: The Long Game: Building Europe’s Sovereign AI Layer
title.fr: The Long Game: Building Europe’s Sovereign AI Layer

speakers.name: Nicolas Flores-Herr
speakers.title: Team Lead Foundation Models, Fraunhofer IAIS

content.en:
OpenGPT-X, TrustLLM, OpenEuroLLM — three projects, three hard lessons in what it actually takes to build foundation models in Europe at scale.
The technical challenges are real, but rarely the ones you’d expect. The governance ones even less so.
This keynote unpacks the journey honestly: where European open-source AI stands today, why the foundational intelligence layer matters more than most policy debates acknowledge, and what building it has taught us about the gap between ambition and craft.
The window is open. The Frontier AI Momentum is still there. The question is whether we’re serious about climbing through it.

title.en: Synthetic Data for the Commons: Building Open SOTA LLMs with Synthetic Environments
title.zh: Synthetic Data for the Commons: Building Open SOTA LLMs with Synthetic Environments
title.fr: Synthetic Data for the Commons: Building Open SOTA LLMs with Synthetic Environments

content.en: Training state-of-the-art language models typically demands vast proprietary datasets and closed pipelines. At Pleias, we take a different path — building open, high-performing LLMs using synthetic data environments designed for the commons. This talk presents our approach to constructing synthetic data pipelines that generate diverse, high-quality training corpora without relying on proprietary sources. We cover the technical architecture behind our synthetic environments, the training strategies that enable competitive performance on standard benchmarks, and why we believe open synthetic data is a critical piece of the puzzle for democratizing access to frontier AI capabilities. We share lessons learned, benchmark results, and a roadmap for community-driven improvements.

title.en: Evaluating Frontier Agents on Economically Valuable Tasks
title.zh: Evaluating Frontier Agents on Economically Valuable Tasks
title.fr: Evaluating Frontier Agents on Economically Valuable Tasks

content.en: It is evident that AI Agents are becoming more and more capable - but what does it take to make them perform well on the real, day-to-day tasks that are prevalent in people’s work? In this presentation I’ll discuss how to model complex environment to evaluate - and improve - agent reliability and performance. I’ll focus on the viability of production deployments in real-world tasks, on the technical side of building and running evals in these cases using Harbor (https://github.com/laude-institute/harbor), and how we are using these techniques at ellamind to build agents that are reliable and provably safe.

title.en: Extension for scikit-learn: Accelerate Workflows with Two Lines of Code
title.zh: Extension for scikit-learn: Accelerate Workflows with Two Lines of Code
title.fr: Extension for scikit-learn: Accelerate Workflows with Two Lines of Code

content.en:
Capabilities of modern hardware are oftentimes underexploited in popular software libraries. Scikit-learn has grown into an industry standard with user-friendly APIs and well-known idioms that users love, but data analytics pipelines oftentimes require a stepup in efficiency and performance.
 
Extension for scikit-learn addresses these gaps by proposing optimized alternatives to selected algorithms without any significant code changes on the user side.
 
This talk will demonstrate how to make machine learning workflows run efficiently by leveraging the UXL Extension for scikit-learn, and will dive into the details of how this works behind the scenes and avenues for future integrations.

title.en: From Agent Traces to Analytics
title.zh: From Agent Traces to Analytics
title.fr: From Agent Traces to Analytics

content.en: Agents continuously produce large volumes of artifacts: code, text, telemetry, etc. Most teams are stuck with static and stale datasets. In 2026, with agents able to create data pipelines as code, fresh and reliable datasets are accessible to any Python coder. We'll share how we built our internal agent evaluation platform with open source Python tools and AI (dlt, LanceDB, Pydantic, Ibis, HuggingFace, and more.)

title.en: Kedro: The Toolbox for Production-Ready Data Pipelines
title.zh: Kedro: The Toolbox for Production-Ready Data Pipelines
title.fr: Kedro: The Toolbox for Production-Ready Data Pipelines

content.en: In this talk, we will explore how software engineering best practices such as modularity, separation of concerns, testability, and reproducibility can elevate the quality and deployability of AI projects. Focussing on the Kedro framework, we’ll uncover how these principles seamlessly integrate into data workflows, making complex projects more manageable and scalable. This session is designed for data practitioners interested in adopting robust software engineering methodologies in their work. Attendees will gain practical insights into improving project design, ensuring code quality, and facilitating smoother transitions to production environments. No extensive software engineering background is required, making this an accessible and informative session for all data professionals looking to enhance their knowledge of software principles through Kedro.

Table foundation models are pretrained to embark implicit priors useful for tables. TabICL is an open and top-performing table foundation model. title.en: The Adoption of the Python Array API in scikit-learn
title.zh: The Adoption of the Python Array API in scikit-learn
title.fr: The Adoption of the Python Array API in scikit-learn

content.en:
The Python array API is a standard API inspired by NumPy's own API that is progressively adopted by array-producing libraries such as NumPy, PyTorch, CuPy, JAX, DPNP on the one hand and array-consuming libraries such as SciPy and scikit-learn on the other hand. Once adopted it will allow scikit-learn to leverage the hardware acceleration support (e.g. GPU support) of the library backing the input arrays instead of always trying to convert those to NumPy and run the computation on the CPU. 

In this presentation, we will give an overview of the adoption of this standard in the scikit-learn library both from a technical point of view and an open source contribution dynamics point of view and then illustrate the performance impacts on some example pipeline.

title.en: Python on GPUs: Speeding Up Machine Learning
title.zh: Python on GPUs: Speeding Up Machine Learning
title.fr: Python on GPUs: Speeding Up Machine Learning

content.en: CUDA Python is a ground up exposure of the CUDA ecosystem in a Pythonic way. By doing this, OSS codes are able to use CUDA directly with supported APIs and languages that are tested the day new hardware is released. OSS codes such as CuPy and PyTorch have adopted this new exposure. Additionally, we released CUDA Tile that makes coding kernels much more akin to working with numpy arrays. We will go through the new exposure and dive into examples of owning your machine learning pipeline with CUDA Python.

title.en: Accelerating scikit-learn with GPUs
title.zh: Accelerating scikit-learn with GPUs
title.fr: Accelerating scikit-learn with GPUs

content.en: Classical ML algorithms -- random forests, logistic regression, PCA, clustering -- remain the backbone of production machine learning. Yet they are often CPU-only. That’s changing. This talk presents two open-source approaches to GPU-accelerating the ML you already use: RAPIDS cuML, which rewrites classical algorithms in CUDA and can transparently accelerate scikit-learn-based libraries like BERTopic with a single import; and scikit-learn’s array API support, which lets the same scikit-learn code run on GPU inputs with no rewrites. Through live demos I’ll show what becomes practical when classical ML goes to the GPU, and offer honest guidance on when to reach for each tool. I maintain both scikit-learn and cuML; this talk reflects what I’ve learned working on both sides.
content.zh: 经典机器学习算法——随机森林、逻辑回归、PCA、聚类——仍然是生产级机器学习的核心支柱。然而，它们通常只能在CPU上运行。这种情况正在改变。本演讲介绍两种开源方法，用于GPU加速您已经在使用的机器学习算法：RAPIDS cuML，它用CUDA重写了经典算法，并可通过单次导入透明地加速基于scikit-learn的库（如BERTopic）；以及scikit-learn的数组API支持，让相同的scikit-learn代码无需改写即可在GPU输入上运行。通过现场演示，我将展示经典机器学习迁移到GPU后能带来哪些新的可能性，并就何时选择哪种工具提供客观的建议。我同时维护scikit-learn和cuML，本演讲正是我在两个项目上工作所积累的经验总结。
content.fr: Les algorithmes de ML classiques -- forêts aléatoires, régression logistique, ACP, clustering -- restent l’épine dorsale du machine learning en production. Pourtant, ils sont souvent limités au CPU. Cela est en train de changer. Cette conférence présente deux approches open source pour accélérer sur GPU le ML que vous utilisez déjà : RAPIDS cuML, qui réécrit les algorithmes classiques en CUDA et peut accélérer de manière transparente les bibliothèques basées sur scikit-learn comme BERTopic avec un seul import ; et le support de l’array API de scikit-learn, qui permet au même code scikit-learn de s’exécuter sur des entrées GPU sans réécriture. À travers des démonstrations en direct, je montrerai ce qui devient pratique lorsque le ML classique passe sur GPU, et offrirai des conseils honnêtes sur quand utiliser chaque outil. Je maintiens à la fois scikit-learn et cuML ; cette conférence reflète ce que j’ai appris en travaillant des deux côtés.

title.zh: SciPy’s Support for GPUs, PyTorch, and CuPy
title.fr: SciPy’s Support for GPUs, PyTorch, and CuPy

content.en: In this talk, I discuss the state of support of GPU computing with "alternative" software array libraries in SciPy via Array API. In addition to user-visible support, I will describe some internal infrastructure of SciPy which might be useful for other libraries, and discuss ongoing work and challenges ahead.

title.en: Skore: Track, Explore, and Share Your Data Science Workflows
title.zh: Skore: Track, Explore, and Share Your Data Science Workflows
title.fr: Skore: Track, Explore, and Share Your Data Science Workflows

content.en:
Skore is the Data Science platform by the scikit-learn founders.
Skore is a data science platform that addresses the challenges of data science in the enterprise world.
Skore helps enterprises adopt AI coding tools reliably, industrialize and scale their data science practice, and bridge the gap between data science and business stakeholders.
Our foundations are the same scientific principles that made scikit-learn the undisputed standard for machine learning, extended now to the team, the organization, and the enterprise.
Tracking, exploring, and sharing data science workflows with skore is as simple and reliable as using scikit-learn!

title.en: notebook.link: Run Notebooks Instantly in Your Browser
title.zh: notebook.link: Run Notebooks Instantly in Your Browser
title.fr: notebook.link: Run Notebooks Instantly in Your Browser

content.en:
As the Founder and CEO of QuantStack - the leading contributor to the Jupyter Project - I present the latest advancements in the Jupyter ecosystem. Key innovations include Jupyter-AI and collaborative editing workflows, but the most transformative is JupyterLite, the most scalable Jupyter distribution, bringing interactive computing to millions of users worldwide.

We introduce the notebook link platform, a powerful solution for sharing Jupyter-based documents at scale, from notebooks and storymaps to CAD models and blog posts. The platform features multi-language support (Python, R, C++, GNU Octave, OCaml, Haskell, SQLite, and more) and an AI assistant workflow with advanced tool-calling capabilities.

A major breakthrough is in-browser tool calling in JupyterLite AI, which brings the full power of Jupyter-AI to lightweight, browser-based workflows. This approach ensures both scalability and enhanced security, as all computations and AI interactions are contained within the browser sandbox.

For education, the platform enables automatic notebook grading and LMS integration, making it ideal for interactive teaching and assessment.

title.en: Skolar and the Value of Curated ML and AI Skills Education
title.zh: Skolar and the Value of Curated ML and AI Skills Education
title.fr: Skolar and the Value of Curated ML and AI Skills Education

content.en: LLMs can write scikit-learn code in seconds, but can you understand what it does? This talk introduces Skolar, an open source free-of-charge learning platform built by scikit-learn's core developers, and makes the case for expert-curated training material as a counter-force to the flood of AI-generated content. Attendees will leave with hands-on exposure to high-quality, structured ML education and a few scikit-learn tricks they probably didn't know.

title.en: What Open Source Communities Can Do to Promote Responsible AI
title.zh: What Open Source Communities Can Do to Promote Responsible AI
title.fr: What Open Source Communities Can Do to Promote Responsible AI

content.en: A fireside chat about responsible open-source AI, from fostering diversity within open-source communities to cutting-edge approaches and open-source tools that can be leveraged to facilitate AI fairness and security. The goal is for each attendee to leave thinking about one tangible action they could realistically take to make their open-source communities more inclusive and welcoming for underrepresented newcomers.

title.en: A2App — Agent Generated Apps using Makepad Splash
title.zh: A2App — 使用 Makepad Splash 生成智能体应用
title.fr: A2App — Applications générées par agent avec Makepad Splash

content.en: In this talk i will show how to rapidly create high performance Rust applications with Makepad. You can use your AI of choice codex, claude running inside the makepad IDE. Rust is the ideal language for AI generation because of its strong compiler guarantees and superb performance. We no longer need to write it by hand. Makepad studio has automation integration for the AI so it can generate, see, click buttons and iterate completely automated on visual applications. Makepad compiles to web, desktop (windows, linux, macos), mobile (android, ios) and XR (Quest). In this talk i will demo how far we can push AI application generation including AI generated CAD, 3D, map rendering, vector engines, and mixed reality 3D world scanning.

title.en: Build Embedded Rust (with AI!)
title.zh: Build Embedded Rust (with AI!)
title.fr: Build Embedded Rust (with AI!)

speakers.name: Bart Massey
speakers.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science, Portland State University

content.en: There has never been a better time to do your embedded work in Rust. Foundational libraries and frameworks have reached reasonable maturity, great tools are available, the Rust language has been improved for embedded use cases, and hardware vendors are officially supporting Rust. The new advances in AI-assisted coding are the icing on the cake — AI works particularly well for embedded Rust: the high standards of Rust code quality and documentation combine with the structured Rust environment to be a safe and effective place for an LLM to work. In this workshop, we will build common new-developer code for the BBC micro:bit v2 using a combination of straight programming and AI assistance.

title.en: Lunch & Learn: What Comes After LLMs? LTMs — The Next Frontier of Enterprise AI
title.zh: 午餐学习会：LLM之后是什么？LTM——企业AI的下一个前沿
title.fr: Lunch & Learn : Après les LLMs ? Les LTMs — La prochaine frontière de l'IA d'entreprise

content.en: LLMs transformed how enterprises work with unstructured data like text, images and code. But what happens when AI needs to reason over the structured data that powers decisions made by the world's most complex businesses? While Large Language Models have redefined how we interact with unstructured data, the vast majority of enterprise data is structured — in millions of rows and columns of tabular data. Large Tabular Models (LTMs) are emerging as a new, specialized class of model designed to bridge this gap. Grab your lunch, and join Fundamental for a Lunch & Learn to learn more about why enterprises are shifting toward LTMs.
